content.text:
I can’t open or change your file from here. Below is a concise, actionable cleanup plan and the exact resulting cell states you should get after standardizing the date display while preserving formulas, validation, and types.

Quick check (before any change)
- Determine whether B2 is stored as text or as a real Excel/Sheets date:
  - Excel/Sheets: enter =ISNUMBER(B2). If TRUE it’s a date serial; if FALSE it’s text.

If B2 is already a real date
1. Select B2.
2. Apply a date number format you prefer (recommended: ISO style): custom format yyyy-mm-dd.
Resulting state:
- B2: value = 2026-07-01 (date serial), Number Format = yyyy-mm-dd (displays 2026-07-01).
- F2: formula =C2*D2 (unchanged). Keep its existing currency number format.
- G2: formula =IF(F2>1000,"Review","OK") (unchanged). Keep its existing cell format and validation.
- Any existing data validation rules remain unchanged.

If B2 is text (shows 2026-7-1 but ISNUMBER(B2) = FALSE)
Option A — Quick in-place conversion (Excel)
1. Select column/row or B2 only.
2. Data → Text to Columns → Delimited → Next → Next → Column data format: Date → choose YMD (or DMY as appropriate for your input) → Finish.
This converts the text to a date serial in-place, preserving cell references and validation.

Option B — Conversion with a helper cell (works in Sheets or Excel)
1. In a spare cell, enter =DATEVALUE(B2) (or =VALUE(B2) in Sheets if DATEVALUE fails).
2. Copy the result, Paste Special → Values back into B2.
3. Set B2 number format to yyyy-mm-dd.
This avoids replacing formulas elsewhere.

Resulting state after conversion (same as above):
- B2: real date 2026-07-01 (date serial), Number Format = yyyy-mm-dd.
- F2: =C2*D2, currency formatting preserved.
- G2: =IF(F2>1000,"Review","OK"), formatting and validation preserved.
- Data validation rules remain in place and intact (if B2 had a date-range rule, converting to a true date makes it enforceable).

Notes and cautions
- Don’t replace B2 with a new formula that references B2 (that would change the cell’s content). Use Text to Columns or paste-values from a helper so B2 ends up as a date value.
- Changing the number format for B2 does not alter formulas in F2/G2 or currency formatting on F2.
- If your locale expects a different date ordering, choose the matching date type (YMD/MDY/DMY) in Text to Columns or ensure you enter 2026-07-01 so it’s unambiguous.

That yields a standardized display of 2026-07-01 in B2 while preserving all formulas, currency formatting, and data validation.
